sources.entry: Snipo - Lightweight, self‑hosted snippet manager for saving and organizing code and text snippets with folders, tags, API, and GitHub Gist sync. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Snipo is a lightweight, self-hosted snippet manager for a single user to store, organize and access code snippets, commands and notes.
summary.what_it_does: Snipo is a self-hosted snippet management system built for one user, protected by a single master password rather than user accounts. The README describes it as a web-based place to keep code fragments, commands and notes, reachable from the terminal, an IDE or a browser. It is deployed by cloning the repository, creating a .env file from the provided example, and starting it with docker compose. The README also points to separate clients: Snippy (a terminal UI), a VS Code extension, and a Chrome/Firefox browser extension. Documentation covers deployment, security model, features, CSS customization, development, an OpenAPI specification and a changelog. The listing text additionally mentions folders, tags, an API and GitHub Gist sync, which the README itself does not detail.
use_cases: Save and organize personal code snippets
Access snippets from terminal, IDE or browser
Self-host a private pastebin for one user
notable: Single-user design with one master password and no user management
Companion clients: Snippy TUI, VS Code extension, Chrome/Firefox browser extension
Docker Compose deployment driven by a .env file
caveats: Designed for a single user only; no multi-user accounts
README advises reading the Deployment Guide before exposing it to the internet
